findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite AC1 to scope 'byte-unchanged' precisely: only the NEW binary contributes 0 to old sidecars; state that debt/moderate/serious lane scores of old sidecars DO change under code-v4 (that is the intended 42→99 effect) and that per-version scoring pins old sidecars to their stored code-v3 result if immutability is actually required.
evidence: AC1: 'old binary-absent sidecars remain byte-unchanged (0 contribution)'
Approach §3 debt: 'churn multiplier becomes AMPLIFIER-ONLY (1.0 + 0.5·min(churn90,30)/30 ∈ [1.0,1.5])' — replaces the code-v3 absent-churn ×0.5, so absent-churn debt findings move 0.5→1.0
Corpus grounding: 'v3 today blocks 42/1243 changes (3.4%); v4 + tests@0.54 blocks 99 (8.0%)' — scores demonstrably change for existing sidecars
findings.finding: AC1's claim that 'old binary-absent sidecars remain byte-unchanged (0 contribution)' contradicts the code-v4 rescoring described in the Approach and the replay numbers. Every pre-existing sidecar lacks the new `forbids_contract_allowed_state` binary, yet the debt-lane churn redesign (absent-churn multiplier changes from ×0.5 to the amplifier floor of exactly 1.0) and the moderate/serious lane splits re-score existing findings — which is the entire mechanism by which blocks rise 42→99. The scores of old sidecars are therefore NOT byte-unchanged; only the NEW binary's contribution is zero.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, line 1 ('old binary-absent sidecars remain byte-unchanged (0 contribution)') vs Approach §3 debt lane + Corpus grounding (42→99 blocks)
scenarios: A reviewer runs the replay expecting old sidecars to hash identically and finds debt-lane and moderate-lane scores shifted, and cannot tell whether that is a bug or intended.
findings.suggested_fix: Split AC1 into two: (a) '`forbids_contract_allowed_state` absent ⇒ 0 contribution to any sidecar's score'; (b) 'old sidecars re-scored under code-v4 reproduce the recorded would-block delta exactly (42→99), NOT byte-identical v3 output' — and remove the misleading 'byte-unchanged' phrasing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the reversibility floor with tests@0.54: either gate the 0.6 floor on lane/tier (exclude the debt lane, or floor debt below 0.54) or state explicitly why a debt-lane finding on a one-way-door surface SHOULD block, and add a unit case (minor debt binary + hard_to_reverse_surface must stay < 0.54).
evidence: decide.py:573-577 — rev_floor = 0.6 when impact_base>0 AND hard_to_reverse_surface; the floor is lane/tier-BLIND
A minor debt binary (dead_code / implicit_coupling, tier _CODE_TIER_MINOR=0.3) yields impact_base>0, so a deletion / released-packaging / schema surface floors impact to 0.6
priority = validity × 0.6 ≈ 0.51–0.57 at the plan's stated 0.85–0.95 validity band → crosses tests@0.54 → BLOCK
A removed/deleted test file is itself a 'deletion' one-way-door surface, so a dead_code/coupling finding on a test-file deletion can floor-and-block
Plan asserts the debt lane 'cannot climb into the block zone' — the unchanged floor defeats that for one-way-door surfaces
findings.finding: The plan keeps the reversibility floor 'unchanged' (0.6, gated only on impact_base>0 AND hard_to_reverse_surface) while lowering the tests threshold to 0.54, which lets a debt-lane finding on a one-way-door surface block — contradicting the plan's stated invariant that debt / hot-file prod=none findings cannot reach the block zone.
findings.location: Approach #3 (code-v4 lane split) — 'debt … churn multiplier becomes AMPLIFIER-ONLY … so hot-file prod=none nits cannot climb into the block zone' and 'Prod lane, detection amp, reversibility floor … unchanged'
scenarios: A refactor deletes an obsolete helper (dead_code) in a released-packaging or schema file; verifier sets no consequence beyond the minor binary; the 0.6 floor blocks it under tests@0.54 despite being intended-advisory
A test-file deletion flagged dead_code floors to 0.6 and blocks
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the reversibility floor so it applies only to the serious/moderate consequence lanes (or set a debt-specific floor below the lowest blocking threshold), and add a v4 unit test asserting a dead_code/implicit_coupling finding on a hard_to_reverse_surface stays advisory under tests@0.54.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the code-review-verify.md (and CodeSeverityAttrs) update that re-scopes prod_impact / trigger_likelihood so the verifier populates them for maintainability/test-coverage findings (not only production consequences), matching code-v4's moderate-lane keying.
evidence: Plan: moderate consequence '... × prod_impact multiplier (high/medium=1.0, low=0.6, none=0.5) × 0.75 when trigger_likelihood=rare — the user-reach keying'
code-review-verify.md L70-71: 'trigger_likelihood (common|sometimes|rare) — how often the PRODUCTION consequence actually triggers in practice'
code-review-verify.md L41-43: 'prod_impact ... none = no runtime effect (docs/test-only/comment)'
verify_models.py L400-405: trigger_likelihood description 'how often the PRODUCTION consequence triggers (prod-lane multiplier ...)'
Approach step 2 only adds `forbids_contract_allowed_state` to code-review-verify.md; no re-scoping of prod_impact/trigger_likelihood is specified though Scope names that prompt
Plan (Context) acknowledges the fields are 'already-answered ... collected and DISCARDED for that lane' — i.e. answered under the PRODUCTION-scoped instructions
findings.finding: code-v4's moderate maintainability lane is keyed on `prod_impact` and `trigger_likelihood`, but the verify prompt and CodeSeverityAttrs schema document both fields as scoping the PRODUCTION consequence only; the plan does not specify re-scoping those field descriptions so the verifier populates them meaningfully for maintainability/test-coverage findings.
findings.location: Approach step 3 (Pass-3 impact model code-v4, moderate consequence bullet) + Scope (code-review-verify.md)
scenarios: A pure test-coverage gap (reachable_path_without_automated_coverage) on test-only code: the prompt tells the verifier prod_impact=none, so the moderate lane multiplies by 0.5 — but the plan's separation argument depends on prod=medium/high on load-bearing test findings, which the current prompt gives no basis to set.
A future contributor edits the verify prompt and cannot tell whether trigger_likelihood should describe production-frequency or maintainability-lane user-reach.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 2/3 and Scope, add that the verify prompt's prod_impact and trigger_likelihood descriptions are amended to state they also key the maintainability lane's user-reach damping (e.g. 'for a coverage/contract finding, prod_impact = the user-facing reach of the path the missing test/broken contract guards'), and note the corresponding field-description edits in verify_models.py.
